task: For this synthetic writing exercise, use the fictional reporting notes to write a reported feature for a general newspaper audience. Write from this reporting snapshot as of April 3, 2025. Include a headline. Target 450 to 650 words. Follow AP style.

facts.text: Alcott County, Texas, is running out of places to put foster children, with 83 children currently housed in hotels, county office suites, and a staff member's private home.

The county's child welfare agency has 847 children in its care and lists 312 licensed foster homes. A home can accommodate more than one child; the notes do not supply total licensed beds or vacancies suitable for particular children.
Agency Director Beverly Chen said: "We are running a de facto shelter system inside a child welfare agency, and that is not what any of these children need."

The Texas Department of State Health and Family Services cited the county in March 2025 for maintaining non-compliant placements and ordered it to reduce the share of children in non-family settings below 10 percent of its total caseload within 90 days.
State Regional Director Raymond Park, who issued the citation, said the county had 90 days to comply or face a potential state receivership of its foster care operations.

With the caseload fixed at 847, fewer than 10 percent means at most 84 children. The regulator counts the 83 current temporary placements as non-family settings, about 9.8 percent. Meeting that numerical threshold does not by itself resolve the citation over non-compliant placement conditions.
The agency has 98 funded caseworker positions but currently has 34 vacancies, a vacancy rate of roughly 35 percent.
Starting caseworker salaries in Alcott County are $41,000 per year; the comparable average in neighboring states is approximately $54,000.
The annual turnover rate for foster families in the county is approximately 28 percent.
Foster parents in Alcott County are reimbursed $29 per day per child; the state average reimbursement is $38 per day.
The county's foster care budget was cut by 12 percent in fiscal year 2024 as part of broader county budget reductions following a property-tax revenue shortfall.

One child in the county's non-compliant placements — referred to in county records as Marcus — is 9 years old and has been living in a hotel for four months; county staff say no family placement has been found that meets his needs.

Alcott County Child Welfare Services signed a contract in January 2025 with Bright Futures Partners, a private child placement firm, to manage the hotel and office placements at a cost of $2.1 million for 18 months.
Chen said the Bright Futures contract was a "stopgap" and that the agency had identified no long-term solution for children it cannot place in family homes.

Texas House Bill 1402, currently before the state legislature, would increase the foster parent daily reimbursement rate to $52 statewide; the bill has passed committee but has not been scheduled for a floor vote.
The agency launched a foster-parent recruitment campaign in February 2025 using paid social media advertising; as of April, it had received 67 inquiries and approved 11 new foster families.

Elena Bell, a child welfare researcher at fictional South Plains College, said recruitment alone would not resolve Alcott County's problems and recommended examining reimbursement and caseworker support. The packet contains no causal evaluation of the county's new campaign.

Alcott County has a population of approximately 210,000; it does not have a homeless shelter, and the hotels being used for foster children are commercial lodging properties billed to the county at market rates.

Chen said her agency had communicated the financial and operational crisis to the county commissioners' court since mid-2023 but had not received additional funds until the state citation in March 2025.
The county commissioners allocated an emergency $750,000 to the agency following the March citation; Chen said the amount was "helpful but not sufficient to resolve the structural problem."
The current licensing process for a new foster home in Alcott County takes an average of seven months, down from a peak of 10 months in 2022.
The Foster Care Reform Alliance called for a state takeover of Alcott County's foster care operations in a statement issued after the March citation.

the state took over Alcott County's foster care operations
the county resolved the shortage by April
